canonical_statement: For every finite-dimensional Brownian Ito SDE on a positive finite horizon, if the deterministic coefficients are jointly measurable, globally Lipschitz and of linear growth and the initial value is square-integrable and independent of future Brownian increments, then a continuous adapted strong solution exists and any two strong solutions are indistinguishable.
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u; P a probability measure; state R^n; noise R^m; time interval [0,T] with T>0
hypotheses: W is an adapted continuous centered Gaussian process with Brownian covariance and independent increments
the initial value is F_0-measurable, square-integrable, and independent of future Brownian increments
b and sigma are jointly measurable, globally Lipschitz in state on [0,T], and satisfy linear growth
the interpretation supplies the standard Bochner time integral and standard Ito integral
conclusion: A continuous adapted strong solution satisfying the integral equation exists, and every two such solutions are indistinguishable on [0,T].
